title: Transition through the target comparison
statement: Let $x$ be a finite Boolean word, $B$ a natural number, and $q$ a rational number. Let $\sigma$ be a register state and $w$ a natural number with $\sigma.tmp=w$, all registers of $\sigma$ at most $B$, $2|x|+2\le B$, and $\sigma.p\le |x|$. If the word of binary digits of $w$ occurs at position $\sigma.p$ in $x$ and ends exactly at the end of $x$, assume that the program started at the target-test stage with pointer $|x|$ and scratch value zero has semantics with acceptance probability $q$. If this occurrence condition fails, assume that for every $p',tmp'\le B$, the program started at the next search stage with pointer $p'$ and scratch value $tmp'$ has semantics with acceptance probability $q$. Then the program started at the target-comparison stage in state $\sigma$ has semantics with acceptance probability $q$.
hypotheses_covered: Every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$
If the binary word of $w$ occurs at $\sigma.p$ and ends at $|x|$, the stated target-test configuration has semantics with acceptance probability $q$
If it does not occur there and end at $|x|$, every next-search configuration with pointer and scratch value at most $B$ has semantics with acceptance probability $q$
replaced:
Let $x$ be a bit string, $B$ a natural number, and $q$ a rational number. Suppose that
$w$ is the scratch-register value of a register state $\sigma$, every register of
$\sigma$ is at most $B$, $2|x|+2\le B$, and the input pointer $p$ of $\sigma$ is at most
$|x|$. If the bits of $x$ starting at position $p$ encode the binary expansion of $w$
and end exactly at the end of $x$, then the program started at the target-test stage
with pointer $|x|$ and scratch value zero has acceptance probability $q$ and satisfies
the termination and register-bound conditions for $B$. If this encoding condition fails,
assume instead that for every $p',w'$ at most $B$, the program started at the next
search stage with those pointer and scratch values has the same semantics with
acceptance probability $q$. Then the program started at the target-comparison stage in
state $\sigma$ has those semantics with acceptance probability $q$.
